18g1w13: A relative clause with the indicative describes a known referent: tengo una habitación que recibe luz. With the subjunctive we present a sought characteristic without asserting that such a referent exists: busco una habitación que reciba luz. The difference is one of perspective, not of size or importance.

zpnbc7: Original SpanishCue text. Read to understand the experience and the decision; then go back to the details.
6icfg4: Three students are looking for an apartment for next school year and have prepared a list that takes up almost a page. They want a place that is near downtown, that has big rooms and that isn't expensive. When they start comparing listings, they discover that no option meets all the conditions. The discussion isn't just about choosing a building; they also need to decide how they want to live together.
y5jni1: Julia cares about having a desk where she can study at night. Omar works from home some days and needs a stable connection. Teresa is concerned about the commute, because she leaves early for her internship. The apartment they saw on Tuesday has good rooms, but is far from public transport. The one they visited on Thursday is smaller and costs a little more, but lets each of them get to their activities without depending on the others.
aufnh9: They don't rule out just any apartment over a minor detail, but they won't accept just any condition either. There are quite a few incomplete listings and some prices are too high for their budget. They will ask before paying any deposit.
1jromad: Instead of voting right away, they separate the essential conditions from the preferences. They discover that the courtyard, which at first seemed fundamental, matters less than quiet and communication with the owner. They also draft three rules on cleaning, visitors and expenses. They haven't signed the contract yet: they want to ask about the deposit and check the condition of the installations. Looking for an ideal apartment has helped them recognize that a workable shared life needs more concrete agreements than a pretty photograph.
